papers.title_in_file: Convex Optimization (Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Cambridge University Press, 2004)
papers.version_note: Seventh printing with corrections, 2009, as stated on the copyright page.
papers.what_it_is: A textbook on convex optimization covering convex sets and functions, duality, applications and interior-point algorithms.

assertions.value: The paper states the separating hyperplane theorem: two nonempty disjoint convex sets can be separated by a hyperplane, with an affine function nonpositive on one set and nonnegative on the other.

assertions.value: The paper proves the separating hyperplane theorem in the special case where the Euclidean distance between the two sets is attained by a pair of points, which holds for example when both sets are closed and one is bounded, and constructs the separating hyperplane as the perpendicular bisector of the segment between the closest points.
quotes: Here we consider a special case, and leave the extension of the proof to the general case as an exercise

assertions.value: The paper states the supporting hyperplane theorem: for any nonempty convex set and any point on its boundary there exists a supporting hyperplane at that point, and notes it follows from the separating hyperplane theorem.
